I will keep the land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou, this is the safest way for me to farm because I know it well, the market is steady, and it fits the local weather and water conditions. I am 73, so I will not choose crops that need too much hand labor or too much market guessing. I will sow winter wheat on all my land first, then after harvest I will plant summer maize on the same fields. I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, because I want stable emergence and stable yield. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and lighter for me than deep ploughing every time. I will put fertilizer in moderate amounts, enough to protect yield but not excessive, because fertilizer is expensive and too much can waste money. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, because wheat in our area usually depends more on timely watering. I will spray pesticides only when needed, mainly to control the common diseases and insects that can cut yield. My goal is not to chase the highest yield. I want a steady harvest, manageable work, and low risk.
